events.name: Mindstone Leeds September AI Meetup
events.description: Explore practical AI, real-world LLM product development and the future of work at Mindstone’s in-person September meetup in Leeds on 28 September 2026. Taking place from **6pm to 9pm** at Barclays Eagle Labs, this monthly meetup brings together people interested in artificial intelligence, its practical applications and the projects shaping how the technology is used. The evening combines technical insight, a hands-on career case study and a broader discussion about AI’s impact on work and society. ## Three perspectives on AI The programme features three talks covering distinct aspects of building with and adapting to AI: - **What I Learned Building With LLMs** — a technical demonstration that breaks down the process of creating an AI-powered product, including practical lessons and real-life insights gained along the way. - **The AI-Powered Career Pivot: An Analyst’s Journey to Consultancy** — Tega Oghoro presents a practical demonstration and step-by-step guide to using AI to make tasks faster and improve their outcomes. - **What Does the Future Look Like With AI?** — a theoretical talk examining how artificial intelligence could affect work, everyday life and wider society. This mix gives attendees the opportunity to see how AI products are built, understand how the technology can support professional development and consider its longer-term implications. The programme will be particularly relevant to AI builders, technologists, analysts, consultants and curious professionals who want to move beyond headlines and learn from concrete projects and experiences. With technical, practical and theoretical sessions on the agenda, attendees can engage with AI from several angles rather than focusing on a single use case. ## Talks, food and community The three-hour event runs **in person** and continues after the presentations with pizza, drinks and networking. This informal part of the evening offers time to discuss the talks, exchange ideas and connect with fellow AI enthusiasts and people exploring new applications of the technology. The meetup is organised by [Mindstone](https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/o/39718183623) and hosted at **Barclays Eagle Labs**, AvenueHQ, 10–12 East Parade, [Leeds](https://www.createwith.com/cities/leeds), LS1 2BH. events.name: From Prototype to Production: Ready for Customers (w/ Baseline and The AI Collective)
events.description:
Tools like Lovable have made it possible for a non-technical founder to ship a working prototype in a night. Getting that prototype in front of paying customers, handling their data safely, and keeping it running when something breaks is a different problem.
Karen Forde, founder of Bridge the Gapp, spends her working week reviewing codebases that founders built with AI tools and no engineering team. She will walk through what she finds, what it costs to fix, and the handful of decisions you can make early that keep a prototype on a path to production.
Hosted by The AI Collective's Dublin chapter and Baseline, this is the follow-on to Pilots & Prototypes. If you built something at Part 1, bring it. If you didn't make Part 1, you're still welcome.
Who this is for:
Founders and operators who have built a prototype with AI tools and are wondering what comes next, along with anyone about to sell, pilot, or raise on something they built themselves. No engineering background needed!

6:00 p.m. - Doors open and networking

7:15 p.m. - Q&A with Karen and non-technical founder
7:30 p.m. - Build time!
8:30 p.m. - Demos and sharing
9:00 p.m. - Close
What to bring:
A laptop and your prototype, if you have one. Questions about your own build are welcome in the clinic.
About the speaker:
Karen Forde is the founder of Bridge the Gapp, a software consultancy working with early-stage founders on code and architecture review, technical direction, and moving AI-built products towards production.

events.name: Miro × n8n hackathon: From diagram to automation
events.description:
Join Miro and n8n for a fast-paced, hands-on hackathon where your best-ignored ideas finally get built. In a few hours, teams go from structured thinking to working automation with the output writing itself back to the board.
Challenge Overview
Come with an existing team, or team-up onsite
Bring a stalled work project, under-resourced idea, or deprioritized workflow that needs improvement
Use Miro to map, align, and design your automation as a visual workflow
Use AI and MCP to build that diagram into a full n8n automation connecting services, triggering actions, and moving data
Have your automation write back to Miro: populating sticky notes, updating boards, or reacting to board activity
Walk away with a working prototype or clear, demonstrable progress
What You'll Do
Design in Miro
Map out your workflow as a diagram. Define the problem, the trigger points, the steps, and the output. Your Miro board is your blueprint and your pitch.
Build in n8n
Turn that diagram into a real automation. Connect the nodes, wire up the services, and make the logic run.
Output back to Miro
Close the loop. Have your n8n workflow write results directly back to your Miro board populating sticky notes, updating cards, or firing actions based on what's happening on the board.
Requirements
Team of four: Must have at least four members on your team to qualify for judging
2.5 min demo: Pitch your problem, walk through your automation, show the Miro output
Miro board : Share your workflow diagram, process map, and final layout
n8n workflow: Exported or shared, showing your automation logic
You'll pitch live to judges. Three teams will walk away the winners receiving standout prizes.
Who Should Join
Product, ops, engineering, and cross-functional teams with real work to unblock
Makers and automators who thrive under constraints and want a breakthrough moment
Anyone who's ever said "we should automate that" and never had the time to do it
events.descriptionSummary: This hands-on hackathon brings together teams to transform their stalled workflows into working automations using Miro's visual mapping and n8n's automation platform, with the finished automations writing results directly back to the board—all in just a few hours with winning teams taking home standout prizes. Teams of four will design their process in Miro, build the automation in n8n, and pitch live to judges, turning those perpetually postponed ideas into demonstrable prototypes.

events.name: From AI Prototype to Production
events.description:
From AI Prototype to Production
What it takes to turn an AI demo into a real product
Building an AI prototype has never been easier.
A few prompts, a model API, some data — and you can have something impressive running in days.
But then reality hits.
Real users. Real data. Real security requirements. Real integrations. Real costs. Real failures.
The gap between an impressive AI demo and a production-ready product is where many teams get stuck.
Join Streamlogic during AI Week SF for a practical session about what it really takes to move from:
AI prototype → production product
We'll explore:
Why AI prototypes are easy to build but difficult to productionize
Where AI products typically break when real users arrive
What needs to be engineered around the model
How to approach AI evaluation and reliability
Data, security, integrations, latency and cost
Where humans should stay in the loop
When AI should assist, recommend or actually execute
How to design AI capabilities that become part of the product rather than another feature
A practical 90-day roadmap from prototype to production
We'll also look at the difference between a simple AI feature and an AI-powered product:
AI feature:
User → prompt → model → response
AI-powered product:
Context → reasoning → rules → tools → action → human feedback → monitoring
No AI hype. No "build an agent in 20 minutes" demo.
Just a practical conversation about the engineering, product and operational decisions that turn an AI experiment into something people can actually rely on.
Who should attend?
This session is for:
Founders
CTOs and technical co-founders
Product leaders
Engineering leaders
AI/ML practitioners
Teams with an AI prototype or pilot that needs to reach production
Already have an AI prototype? Bring it.
We'll discuss what needs to happen between "it works in a demo" and "we can trust it in production."
This event is part of AI Week SF 2026.
events.descriptionSummary: Streamlogic will break down the real engineering work behind moving AI prototypes from impressive demos to dependable products, covering everything from data pipelines and security to human-in-the-loop decisions and reliability testing—without the hype. Founders, CTOs, product leaders, and engineering teams working on AI projects will walk through a practical 90-day roadmap for turning an AI experiment into something users can actually trust.

events.name: Book Launch—Foreign Policy at the AI Frontier: How AI is Reshaping Progress, Power, and Peace”
events.description:
Space is limited so make sure to arrive early to guarantee a seat.
Join us on September 28th, from 4:30 to 6:00pm for the launch of Branka Panic’s new book “Foreign Policy at the AI Frontier: How AI is Reshaping Progress, Power, and Peace.” Organized around three themes—Progress, Power, and Peace—the book explores how AI is reshaping the future of foreign policy.
It takes readers from the history of diplomatic technology, the frontiers of agentic diplomacy, and the Global South's growing role in shaping AI's future. The book blends case studies with ethical reflection to equip its readers to act where two frontiers meet:  the technological and the diplomatic.
This event is co-hosted by NYU Center on International Cooperation, NYU Peace Research and Education Program, and Data for Peace.
Light refreshments will be served.
About the Author
Founder and Executive Director at AI for Peace | Author on AI, Peace and Foreign Policy | TEDx and International Keynote Speaker | Strategic Adviser
Branka Panic is the founder, author, speaker, and advisor to governments, UN agencies, and civil society, navigating the responsible use of AI for peace and security. A keynote speaker and author of the foundational book AI for Peace, and the blog series Is AI Coming in Peace?, she has helped shape the global discourse on how artificial intelligence can prevent conflict, safeguard human rights, and advance lasting peace. She works with AI both as a topic of policy debate and as a hands-on tool for diplomacy and peacebuilding. She is a Non-Resident Fellow at NYU-CIC, and one of the organizers of the Data for Peace Conference.
events.descriptionSummary: Branka Panic will launch *Foreign Policy at the AI Frontier*, exploring how AI will reshape progress, power, and peace through diplomatic history, agentic diplomacy, and the Global South’s influence. A Non-Resident Fellow at NYU’s Center on International Cooperation and founder of AI for Peace, Panic advises governments, UN agencies, and civil society on responsible AI for peace and security.

events.name: Token Economics: Why Cost Kills More AI Projects Than Hallucinations
events.description: Token costs have overtaken hallucinations as the top reason enterprise AI projects die before reaching production; it’s cited by 29% of technical leaders as the primary production killer, ahead of every reliability failure combined. The teams seeing success don't treat inference cost as an after-the-fact line item. They architect for token costs from the beginning. ​This event examines what that shift actually looks like in practice: GPU memory and data architecture decisions that determine cost per token served and the orchestration choices that separate a project that survives its second budget review from one that doesn't. ​We'll open with new VentureBeat Pulse Research on how enterprises are — and aren't — measuring the economics of the AI they're already running. ​This isn't a panel. It's a small group of peers, over drinks, working through the hardest question in enterprise AI right now. An evening conversation and drinks with a small number of enterprise AI leaders, kept intentionally close to keep the conversation substantive. ​**Applications reviewed on a rolling basis — apply today to request one of the remaining seats**

events.name: AISecEng Chicago Launch: Modern AI Security Practices & Windows 11 Defense
events.description: Join us for the inaugural meetup of the **AI Security Engineering Community (AISecEng) – Chicago Chapter!** We are kicking off our very first event with a double feature lineup of expert speakers to cover modern AI security practices and OS-level defense. **Session 1: AI Acceleration & Security Engineering** *Speaker:* **Micah Silverman**, Director of AI Acceleration at Snyk As organizations rapidly integrate artificial intelligence and generative tools into their development workflows, security engineering paradigms are shifting fast. Micah will share insights from the front lines of AI acceleration, covering: * **The Evolving AI Landscape**: Key trends driving AI adoption in software engineering and the emerging security considerations accompanying them. * **Risk & Acceleration**: How engineering teams can adopt modern AI capabilities safely without introducing unnecessary organizational risk. * **Modern AI Security Practices**: Strategic approaches to managing security, privacy, and integrity in AI-enhanced environments. **Session 2: Security Features in Windows 11** *Speaker:* **Dan Rey,** Productivity Solutions Analyst at McDonald's In this talk, Dan Rey will share stories of security features Microsoft introduced to assist in making Windows much more secure by default, giving administrators the ability to lock down windows end points and push the devices to be managed by cloud identities instead of local accounts Dan will cover: * Out of Box Experience (OOBE) in Windows 11 * AppLocker and Windows 11 S mode * Windows Sandbox * Key issues, legacy surface area, and exploits addressed in recent Windows updates **Networking & Q&A** Connect with local Chicago AI security engineers, application security professionals, and developers after the talks. Whether you are an AppSec professional, software engineer, or technical leader navigating the adoption of AI technologies, this event offers a great opportunity to learn, share insights, and connect with the local community. **Event Details** * **Date**: Monday, September 28, 2026 * **Time**: 6:00 PM CDT * **Location**: AON Building, 200 E Randolph St, Suite 200, Chicago, IL * **\*\*\*IMPORTANT\*\*\***: Photo ID required to enter the building. events.name: UK AI Conference in Nottingham for Early Career Researchers & PhD Students
events.description: The Fourth UK AI Conference returns to [Nottingham](https://www.createwith.com/cities/nottingham) this September, bringing together early career researchers and PhD students working at the cutting edge of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data science. Taking place 29-30 September 2026 at the Hilton Nottingham, this conference is uniquely organised by early career researchers for their peers, creating an environment where emerging talent can share work, build networks, and shape the future of AI research in the UK. ## What Makes This Conference Special This isn't your typical academic conference. The UK AI Conference is designed specifically for early career researchers and PhD students, providing a supportive platform to present research, receive feedback from peers, and connect with fellow researchers across multiple AI disciplines. The 2026 edition is supported by the Turing AI Fellowship: Somabotics Creatively Embodying AI, led by the [University of Nottingham](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/computerscience/), ensuring high-quality academic standards whilst maintaining an accessible, collaborative atmosphere. ## Submission Opportunities The call for papers is now open, with two submission pathways designed to accommodate different stages of research: **Full Papers** — For researchers ready to deliver a talk and publish their work in the Proceedings of Machine Learning Research (PMLR) as part of the official conference proceedings. This pathway offers the opportunity to add a peer-reviewed publication to your academic portfolio whilst presenting to an engaged audience of fellow researchers. **Abstracts** — Perfect for poster presentations showcasing ongoing or emerging research. This format is ideal for getting feedback on work in progress, testing ideas, and sparking collaborative discussions with other attendees working in related fields. ## Who Should Attend This conference is designed for early career researchers and PhD students working in AI, data science, machine learning, or related computational fields. Whether you're exploring computer vision, natural language processing, robotics, responsible AI, or any other AI subdomain, you'll find a community of peers facing similar challenges and pursuing complementary research goals. Supervisors of PhD students are also encouraged to attend and support their researchers' development. ## Networking and Community Beyond the formal presentations, the UK AI Conference serves as a crucia
events.descriptionSummary: The Fourth UK AI Conference will bring together early career researchers and PhD students to present cutting-edge work in AI and machine learning, with submissions accepted for both full papers (publishable in PMLR) and poster presentations—all organized by early-career researchers themselves to foster genuine peer collaboration and community building.

events.name: Hard Things
events.description:
Hard Things is back.
We’re excited to return to our community of physical AI founders, investors, and ecosystem partners with Chris Yeh.
Chris Yeh is the co-author of Blitzscaling, the book that explains how to build world-changing companies like Amazon, Alibaba, and Airbnb in record time.
A writer, investor, and entrepreneur, Chris has had a ringside seat in the world of startups and scaleups since 1995. His books help founders, venture capitalists, corporate leaders, policymakers, and everyday people better understand how the internet has changed the way we work together to build amazing organizations.
As a reminder, Hard Things is an invite-only event series organized by Mavka Capital with the support of Foley & Lardner LLP, dedicated to the innovators and breakthroughs shaping Physical AI — the shift from cloud-based intelligence to AI embodied in machines and real-world systems.

events.name: AI Agents for Data Teams: A Practical Mini-Hackathon
events.description:
Bring a real problem. Build something useful. Show what works.
Join the Bay Area Snowflake User Group for an evening building with Snowflake’s agentic AI products.
Find the right data, access it appropriately, improve documentation, check quality or govern how it is used. No problem is too small if solving it adds value to your team.
Come solo and find collaborators, or bring a team of up to four. Leave with experience collaborating on Snowflake’s agentic AI products, something you built and tested, and an explanation of what improved.
Planned products
Explore Snowflake CoCo for building, Cortex Agents for working with governed data and tools, and Snowflake CoWork as the conversational workspace. A planned Cognee integration example explores memory for Snowflake agents. Final walkthrough and account preparation details will be shared before the session.
The evening
5:00 PM: Arrive & find your team
5:30 PM: Welcome & a practical starting point
5:45 PM: Build with Snowflake’s agentic AI products
7:15 PM: Show what works & share what you learned
8:00 PM: Wrap up
How we’ll review the work
Value Creation: Does it add value to a team?
Innovation: Are you using the tools in new ways?
Working: How much did you build and get running?
Partners & support
Snowflake is the lead sponsor. Cognee sponsors the session with its focus on memory for AI agents, and Dave Nielsen supports teams. Silicon Valley AI Hub is the venue host. Organized with support from Milbird.
What to bring
A laptop and a real data-team task. Use public, synthetic or approved sample data you can share with your team.
events.descriptionSummary: Data engineers and AI enthusiasts will spend an evening hands-on with Snowflake's agentic AI suite—building practical solutions to real data challenges using CoCo, Cortex Agents, and CoWork, then showcasing what actually works. Bring a genuine problem from your team and leave with a working prototype and fresh experience collaborating on AI-powered data tools.

events.name: Big Data & AI World Asia | Tech Week Singapore

- **Learn from senior data and AI practitioners** sharing real-world case studies. - **Explore emerging technologies** and their business applications. - **Network with the community** driving Asia’s data and AI transformation. ### Registration [Register now on the official event page](https://www.singaporetechnologyweek.com/big-data-ai-world) to secure your spot. *Follow Big Data & AI World Asia on [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/BigDataAIWorldSG), [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/big-data-world), [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCmsF9E7rxx0UWsDd8P0Wg4A/videos), and [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/techweeksingapore) for updates.*
events.descriptionSummary: Asia's data and AI leaders from FedEx, McKinsey, Airwallex, and other major organizations will converge for a two-day deep dive into how AI and big data are transforming business strategy and operations across industries.
